digest.component_or_area: plan review sizing and model escalation
propositions: When a plan review trips a provider context limit, the Pass-1 finder escalates to a bare Anthropic model ID, bypassing the model-class table and silently relocating calls away from the configured provider (e.g., Bedrock to direct Anthropic).

The _rung_target function compares rung class resolution against provider inference using only the ladder constant, never considering the run's actual configured model, causing provider-qualified models to degrade to bare Anthropic family names.

On Bedrock-qualified primaries with no class table configured, models_at_or_above returns bare Anthropic identifiers instead of preserving the Bedrock provider qualifier, and subsequent replace(cfg, model=bare_id) produces invalid Bedrock model IDs.

The one-criterion retry on an entry rung named 'frontier' executes the incorrect substitution path before any rare deep-escalation case occurs, affecting all context-limit escalations not just uncommon scenarios.

The fix threads the run's primary model into _rung_target to apply provider-agreement logic: providers agree or either is undeterminable, return today's value; providers differ on primary's own rung, return primary verbatim; providers differ on higher rung, drop the rung and surface the too_big failure instead of crossing providers.
